newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Ann Joo plans to be integrated steel firm.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Ann Joo plans to be integrated steel firm.

text.p: Malaysian steel company Ann Joo Resources Bhd, which is due to be listed on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange this month, said on Tuesday that it aims to become an integrated steel maker within the next five years.

"We hope to be an integrated steel producer within three to five years, which would include making our own billets," Ann Joo executive director Lim Boon Hiong told Reuters after an analysts' briefing on Tuesday.
Currently, Ann Joo buys its steel billets which form the basis of its manufactured hot-rolled products, from Perwaja Steel Sdn Bhd, which Lim said is planning to produce its own value-added products.
"They may decide to use their (billets) production for their own activities, and so they may not be able to supply us in the future," said Lim.
Ann Joo is offering 20.23 million shares at 2.00 ringgit a share and expects to list its stock this month. Its products are used in the automotive, electronics and construction industries.

"By being integrated we would save on the transportation costs of bringing the billets to us. We would also be able to put the billets straight through to the manufacturing process without having to reheat them," said Lim.
The group began its operations 50 years ago as a trader of steel products. Ann Joo's trading arm still contributes around 50 percent of the group's turnover, executives said.
At the briefing, Ann Joo executives also detailed plans to expand into downstream products like galvanising wire, wire mesh, cold drawn wire and fasteners.
Ann Joo executives said they anticipated group turnover to increase by around 10 percent over the next two years, while net profits should rise by around 15 percent.
In 1995, the company reported turnover of 309.63 million and net profit of 22.23 million ringgit.
Executives said they hoped to achieve the gains through cost cuts and increased productivity.

"I'm looking at a fair value of around 4.50 for the stock," said Ramlan Ahmad, senior manager at fund managers Commerce MGI Sdn Bhd after the briefing. "That would translate to a price-to earnings multiple of around 20 times based on (estimated) 1997 earnings," he added.
"I think with a paid up capital of 151 million ringgit, it is not too illiquid for institutional interest," added Ramlan.

Ann Joo's subsidiary and associated companies are involved in making hot rolling of long products mainly of steel sections, round and deformed bars, cast iron products, the shearing and slitting of flat products and precision metal stamping.
The company's capacity is 200,000 tonnes a year and it has government approval to raise that eventually to 750,000 tonnes.
